security_privacy_cost_impact: The RFC records a security consequence rather than creating one: option A makes app_command reachable by anyone able to sign a JWT with the project secret, which is the same holder who can already claim service_role and bypass RLS entirely. Nothing in this increment grants anything.
migration_and_data_impact: None. The migration this RFC proposes is named in §5 and belongs to WP-0A-DB-00, which will write it if and when the Product Owner disposes this.
compatibility_impact: None. Two Proposed decision records and their work package. No migration, no lint rule, no grant. RFC-2026-019 supersedes RFC-2026-018 and neither ever changed the tree.
known_limitations: RFC-2026-019 is Proposed and awaits Product Owner disposition. This run wrote it and may not dispose its own decision.

RFC-2026-018 is Approved and superseded, and its status line still says only Approved. Recording the supersession is a decision-record status change and belongs to a disposition branch, not to this one. Until that happens the repository holds an approved decision that must not be implemented, and that is the most dangerous shape a record can have here.

The three lint rules RFC-2026-019 §5 names are not written. They belong to WP-0A-DB-00. Two of them assert states measured true today -- authenticator holds no service-role membership, and app_command owns no table in app -- so they are assertable immediately rather than someday.
A1 has not seen this RFC. Its countersignature identified the gap -- the topology is built and not connected -- but identifying a gap is not agreeing with a proposal for filling it.

rollback_or_forward_fix: Revert through a reviewed revert PR. Reverting removes the correction and leaves an approved decision that must not be implemented, which is worse than either document alone.
reviewer_instructions: Read RFC-2026-019 §1 against RFC-2026-017 §3 directly. The whole correction turns on one line: app_command OWNS the SECURITY DEFINER command functions, so it is not a role a caller switches to.
§1's comparison table is the argument. If granting app_command to authenticator is a narrowing against the design rather than against service_role, the correction is wrong and RFC-2026-018 stands.
Nothing in the tree implements either RFC. If you find a grant or a migration in this diff, that is the defect.
